newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end mixed, fronts hold chart gains.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end mixed, fronts hold chart gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures ended mixed Monday in a sluggish session, with front months holding modest technical gains but many sidelined waiting for clearer cash signs to emerge when Oct flows begin.
November gained 3.3 cents to close at $2.214 per million British thermal units. December settled 2.9 cents higher at $2.384. Others were mixed, with 1998s losing ground.

"We settled at the higher end of the range, so we could see a higher open tomorrow, but this was a technical rally and there's not a lot of load," said one Midwest trader, noting storage demand alone was not enough to support prices.
Most fundamental traders were wary of further gains, noting storage injections were likely to slow next month and demand was typically-slack in an autumn shoulder month.
But technically, traders said November's close above $2.21 could soon lead to a test of next resistance at the $2.305 recent high. They still pegged support in the low-$2 area.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices notionally firmed slightly Monday to near the $1.90 level. October Midcon prices were pegged steady in the mid-$1.70s. New York city gate gas was quoted in the $2.16-2.20 range, also little changed from Friday.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 1.2 cents to $2.122. NYMEX said 23,717 Hub contracts traded, up from Friday's revised tally of 18,922.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled up one-half cent at 99.5 cents, while deferreds closed steady to two cents higher.
NYMEX November Permian natgas ended with a four-cent gain at $1.86, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX said 19 Permian lots changed hands versus no trading on Friday.

On the KCBT, November settled three cents higher at $1.97, while deferreds ended steady to up 2.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 0.3 cent to 24.4 cents (NYMEX premium). --J Silha, New York Power Desk 212-859-1624
